To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of chitinolytic clostridia in the culture medium of cellulolytic anaeroic fungi significantly depressed their cellulolysis.

the presence of chitinolytic Clostridia in the rumen can inhibit the growth and cellulolytic activity of anaerobic fungi and that this inhibition is probably mediated by soluble products of chitin degradation.
the presence of rumen chitino lytic bacteria in co culture with cellulolytic fungi significantly depressed the cellulolysis by these fungi.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interactions between cellulolytic bacteria and fungi in rumen.
the study of ruminal anaerobic fungi, which play an important role in the degradation of plant cell wall carbohydrates.
the effect of rumen bacteria on the cellulolytic activity of rumen anaerobic fungi, and the effect of the fungi on the activity of cellulolytic bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rumen chitin degrading bacteria may inhibit the cellulolytic activity of anaerobic fungi, and this may be due to the production of a factor which is inhibitory to fungal cellulases.
the presence of the chitinolytic Clostridial strain ChK5 in the rumen environment could lead to a decrease in the efficiency of cellulolytic anaero­bic fungi in the degradation of plant cell walls.
the rumen chitino-lytic bacteria are capable of producing a variety of chitinolytic enzymes, which may have a significant effect on the growth and metabolism of rumen anaerobic fungi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chitinase producing bacteria may inhibit the activity of cellulolytic fungi.
chitinase producing rumen bacteria can inhibit the cellulolytic activity of rumen fungi.
rumen chitinase producing bacteria can inhibit the growth and activity of cellulolytic anaeroic fungi in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
some bacteria that are able to degrade chitin are also able to degrade cellulose.
chitinolytic microbes may have a negative effect on the cellulolytic activity of anaerobic fungi, and that the effect may be more pronounced in the case of fungi with multiple nuclei.
